markdown_report:
The strongest next step is a **catalog competition audit** of each category’s single NextItNet checkpoint. At 0% research progress, this offers a practical way to distinguish weak target separation from competition that supplied negatives miss.

Three insights follow from the supplied diagnosis. First, Electronics has 9.38% negative-over-positive outcomes, versus 0.23–3.91% elsewhere. This identifies weaker measured training separation, without establishing worse validation ranking. Second, frequency-matched old substitutions are less disruptive than random substitutions in Movies and CDs. Their absolute margin changes remain negative, so the evidence does not justify discarding older history. Third, padding activations were zero on observed batches. Locality remains uncertified, so further architectural conclusions require additional checks.

Three literature insights guide the next investigation. Krichene and Rendle show that sampled metrics can change model comparisons; supplied-negative success therefore cannot certify catalog retrieval. Prakash et al. report frequency-dependent performance differences, motivating training-frequency strata. NextItNet’s causal convolutions preserve sequential structure, making prefix-based competition measurements compatible with the required backbone; they do not establish user intent.

These insights define three directions: candidate competition, temporal mechanism, and evidence sufficiency. The framework separates what each direction measures:

| Direction | Measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Competition | Exact training-prefix target rank | Generalization |
| Temporal mechanism | Controlled lag or activation intervention | Whether retraining helps |
| Evidence sufficiency | Title/description support and abstention | Actual intent or satisfaction |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessments |
|---|---|---|
| Catalog competition audit [1,2] | 4/7/3 | Originality: useful diagnostic combination, established components. Potential: exposes missed competitors, training ranks may be optimistic. Difficulty: existing scoring interface suffices, catalog scans cost inference. |
| Block activation patching [3,4] | 5/6/6 | Originality: family-specific adaptation, established intervention. Potential: localizes sensitivity, restoration does not prove necessity. Difficulty: hooks avoid retraining, downstream recomputation needs careful controls. |
| Evidence-and-abstention records [5] | 4/6/4 | Originality: useful recommendation adaptation, existing annotation principles. Potential: separates unsupported claims, cannot recover latent intent. Difficulty: public text suffices, reliable annotation needs calibration. |

Select the **catalog competition audit**. Freeze each model and evaluate reproducible training prefixes with their next observed training item. Gather the final nonpadding feature, score eligible catalog items in chunks, retain the target, and exclude prefix-seen alternatives. Count strictly higher-scoring competitors and report ties separately. Compare exact rank with supplied-negative separation; summarize target-minus-tenth-competitor margins by prefix length and training-frequency band.

Preserve the diagnostic interfaces and report counts, definitions, and missing reasons. These are fitting diagnostics; only pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects models. No additional predictor, architecture change, or inferred compatibility signal is required.

References: [1] Krichene–Rendle; [2] Prakash et al.; [3] NextItNet; [4] Heimersheim–Nanda; [5] evidence-sufficiency protocol. Links appear below.

idea.description: Add a bounded exact-catalog competition audit to the existing family-aware NextItNet diagnostic adapter. For reproducible training prefixes, compare supplied-negative separation against target rank among eligible catalog items using the same frozen checkpoint. Report frequency and history-length strata without fitting another predictor.
idea.motivation: The supplied measurements show substantial differences in training pairwise separation, particularly Electronics’ 9.38% negative-over-positive rate. They do not reveal how many catalog items outrank an observed target. Previous lag interventions demonstrate relative temporal sensitivity rather than harmful older history. Catalog competition is a complementary, feasible diagnostic that avoids turning qualitative feedback into unsupported assumptions about ownership, compatibility, or intent.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions; explicitly distinguish training-prefix catalog measurements from host validation metrics. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces.

Use only training histories and aligned next-training-item targets. Cache at most ten loader batches; reproducibly select at most 128 valid rows per category using a local seed-42 generator. Disclose that loader sampling may repeat users; without reliable user identity, report row-level summaries without user-bootstrap confidence intervals. Save and restore the actual module’s training mode, disable gradients, and score in deterministic evaluation mode.

Gather features at the largest occupied sequence index, never occupied_count-1. Exclude empty histories and invalid aligned targets with explicit counts. For supplied-negative comparisons require a valid, distinct negative; catalog measurements may still proceed when that negative is unavailable. Exclude ID 0 and prefix-seen alternatives while retaining the target even when repeated in the prefix. Label this as a prefix-seen filtering protocol: truncated inputs do not establish the entire observed history.

Score items through predict_score in bounded chunks, for example 4,096 IDs, avoiding a rows-by-entire-catalog allocation. Accumulate counts of scores strictly greater than and equal to the target score, excluding the target itself. Report the optimistic rank 1+greater and pessimistic rank 1+greater+ties, rank percentiles with eligible-catalog denominators, and corresponding top-10 hit bounds. Maintain only the ten highest competing scores per row to calculate target-minus-tenth-competitor margin; mark it missing when fewer than ten alternatives exist. Reject nonfinite rows with counted reasons.

Compute item-frequency bands exclusively from user_train['History'], keeping tied frequencies together and reporting realized bin sizes. Report length strata 1–5, 6–15, 16–31, and 32+, with counts and empty-cell reasons. Describe higher-ranked unobserved items as competitors, not verified negatives. Training targets may already have influenced model fitting; these measurements do not estimate generalization or establish recommendation satisfaction.

Keep the supplied corrected cold-start NextItNet training and predictor writer unchanged. Train one independent checkpoint per category, preserving all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Load exactly one checkpoint per category at prediction. Bound diagnostic runtime within the shared search budget. Do not reconstruct hidden validation candidates, access test data, reuse other trials, or introduce score fusion. No implementation or new experiment was executed for this proposal.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    previous_mode = self.view.model.training
    metrics, definitions = {}, {}
    try:
        self.view.model.eval()
        rows = cache_and_select_rows(train_loader, max_batches=10,
                                     max_rows=128, local_seed=42)
        frequency_bands = bands_from_training_histories_only()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for sequence, positive, negative in rows:
                last = largest_index_where(sequence != 0)
                if last is missing:
                    count_exclusion('empty_history'); continue
                target = positive[last]
                if not valid_catalog_id(target):
                    count_exclusion('invalid_target'); continue
                feature = self.view.log2feats(sequence)[last]
                target_score = score(feature, target)
                greater, ties, eligible = 0, 0, 1
                top_competitors = empty_topk(k=10)
                seen = set(nonzero_ids(sequence))
                for items in catalog_chunks(size=4096):
                    alternatives = [i for i in items
                                    if i != target and i not in seen and i != 0]
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(feature, alternatives)
                    verify_finite_or_exclude_row(scores)
                    greater += count(scores > target_score)
                    ties += count(scores == target_score)
                    eligible += len(alternatives)
                    top_competitors.update(scores)
                record(rank_lower=1 + greater,
                       rank_upper=1 + greater + ties,
                       eligible_count=eligible,
                       margin_to_tenth=target_score - top_competitors.tenth_or_missing(),
                       frequency_band=frequency_bands[target],
                       length_band=band(count_nonzero(sequence)))
                if valid_distinct_negative(negative[last], target):
                    record_supplied_negative_margin(feature, target, negative[last])
        summarize_with_counts_missing_reasons_and_protocol_definitions()
    finally:
        self.view.model.train(previous_mode)
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embeds both dictionaries,
# requests evidence-linked findings, and explicitly separates training
# competition from validation quality and unobserved user intent.

originality.positive: Connects family-specific training diagnostics with exact catalog competition and explicit tie bounds, complementing the earlier lag-ablation work.
originality.negative: Exact ranking, frequency stratification, and sampled-metric cautions are established techniques; the contribution is their integration.

future_potential.positive: Can identify whether a future single-model experiment should target candidate discrimination or frequency-dependent fitting while preserving NextItNet.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix competition can be optimistic and may not predict improvements on the pinned validation benchmark.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses existing ModelView scoring methods and requires no retraining, architectural modification, or predictor change.
code_difficulty.negative: Catalog scans require bounded memory and runtime, careful filtering, and explicit handling of ties, invalid rows, and repeated users.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
Motivates distinguishing supplied-negative separation from catalog competition.
limitations: Does not establish that catalog training diagnostics predict held-out performance.
Does not justify altering the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Prakash et al.: sequential recommendation, negative sampling, and popularity imbalance
contributions: The supplied search summary reports performance differences across item-frequency groups and sensitivity to negative sampling.
Motivates reporting training-frequency strata rather than aggregate margins alone.
limitations: Its reported findings are not measurements of the supplied NextItNet checkpoints.
Frequency strata do not explain individual user intent.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual causal dilated convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the required backbone family for the proposed diagnostic.
limitations: Architecture alone does not certify every functional dependency in a modified implementation.
Does not establish the proposed catalog-audit protocol.

related_work.title: Heimersheim and Nanda: activation patching guidance
contributions: Distinguishes restoration and disruption interpretations of activation patching.
Informs the alternative block-patching research direction.
limitations: Transfer to sequential recommendation requires validation.
Restoration does not prove necessity or unique information storage.

related_work.title: Evidence relevance and sufficiency annotation protocol
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separating relevance, support, and insufficient evidence.
Informs recommendation evidence records that explicitly allow abstention.
limitations: Is not a validated Amazon recommendation rubric.
Textual evidence annotations cannot establish ownership, satisfaction, or latent purchasing needs.
